stages.title: Advanced grammar
stages.hook: English says "I put the book on the table". Mandarin can move the object in front of the verb with 把. Why would it do that?
explain: The 把 (bǎ) construction puts the object before the verb to show what is done to it and what happens to it: 我把书放在桌子上 (I put the book on the table). The verb usually has a result, direction or place after it, so 我把书放 alone sounds unfinished.

The 被 (bèi) construction is a passive: 杯子被弟弟打破了 (the cup was broken by younger brother). It was once used mostly for unpleasant events, but is now also used for neutral ones. The 比 (bǐ) construction compares: 今天比昨天冷 (today is colder than yesterday), with no 很 before the adjective.
Other patterns include 越来越 (yuèláiyuè, more and more), 一…就… (as soon as) and 连…都… (even). 是…的 emphasises details of a past event: 我是昨天来的 (it was yesterday that I came).
stages.mnemonic: 把 grabs the object and moves it in front of the verb.
sentences: I put the book on the table.
The cup was broken by my brother.

gq.why: The 把 object must come before the verb, and the verb needs a complement.

gq.q: How do you say "Today is colder than yesterday"?
gq.why: 比 goes between the two things, and no 很 is used.

panel.q: Why is 我把书看 incomplete?
o: 把 cannot be used with books
The verb needs a result or complement
panel.why: A 把 sentence normally needs a result or complement after the verb, such as 完.

panel.q: What does 越来越 add in 天气越来越冷?
panel.why: It shows an increasing change: more and more.

panel.q: What does 我是昨天来的 emphasise?
o: The time of the past event
panel.why: The 是…的 pattern focuses on a detail of an event already happened, here the time.

teach.model: 把 brings the object before the verb and needs a result after the verb. 被 makes a passive. 比 compares two things without 很. 是…的 highlights a detail of a past event.

trip.prompt: Find the page on the ba-construction and read one example.

stages.title: Complex sentence patterns
stages.hook: What if you want to say "even if it rains, we will go" or "only if you practise will you improve"? Let us build conditions.
explain: Intermediate learners use many paired patterns. 即使…也… (even if… still…): 即使下雨，我们也去. 只要…就… (as long as… then…): 只要努力就会进步 means as long as you work hard you will improve. 只有…才… (only if… then…): 只有坚持才能成功 means only by persisting can you succeed.
无论…都… (no matter… still…): 无论天气怎么样，我们都去. 既…又… (both… and…): 她既聪明又勤奋. 与其…不如… (rather than… better…): 与其等，不如自己去. 尽管…还是… means despite, still.

Distinguishing 只要 and 只有 is important. 只要 gives a sufficient condition, so one thing is enough. 只有 gives a necessary condition, so there is no other way. This is a typical point of grammar assessment.
stages.mnemonic: 只要 is enough, 只有 is the only way.
sentences: As long as you work hard you will improve.
Only by persevering can you succeed.
No matter the weather, we all go.

gq.why: 只有…才… expresses a necessary condition.

gq.q: What does 既聪明又勤奋 say?

panel.q: Which is a sufficient condition (one thing is enough)?
panel.why: 只要…就… means as long as, so it is enough.

panel.q: Why would 只有努力才能成功 be stronger than 只要努力就能成功?
o: It says hard work is the only way
panel.why: 只有 says hard work is necessary, while 只要 says it is enough.

panel.q: What does 与其坐车，不如走路 suggest?
panel.why: 与其…不如… shows a better choice.

teach.model: 只要…就… says one condition is enough. 只有…才… says it is the only way. 无论…都… means no matter what, and 即使…也… means even if. Each pair is used together.

points.ask: And what does 只有 mean?
How do I say no matter what?

trip.prompt: Find the list of conjunction pairs and write one new sentence with each.

stages.title: Extended conversations
stages.hook: In a real conversation you agree, disagree, and change topics. Which small words make that smooth?
explain: Conversation fillers keep talk natural. 其实 (qíshí) means actually, 不过 (búguò) means however, 当然 (dāngrán) means of course and 对了 (duìle) means by the way. To give an opinion use 你觉得…呢？ to ask others and 我的看法是… to answer.

To agree, say 我同意 (I agree) or 没错 (right). To disagree politely, soften your language: 我不太同意 (I don't quite agree) or 不一定 (not necessarily), instead of a blunt 你错了. 说实话 (shuōshíhuà) means to be honest.
Listening matters too. Show you follow with 嗯, 对, or 是吗？ (really?). A good conversation takes turns, and uses questions like 你呢？ to give the other person space.
stages.mnemonic: Soften before you disagree: 我不太同意.
sentences: Actually, I don't quite agree with you.
What do you think of this method?
By the way, are you free tomorrow?

gq.why: 不太同意 is a gentler way to disagree.

gq.q: What does 对了 do at the start of a sentence?
gq.why: 对了 introduces a new topic: by the way.

panel.q: Why do speakers say 其实 before a different opinion?
o: It makes the sentence a question
panel.why: 其实 means actually, and gently introduces a different view.

panel.q: A friend says 不一定. How would you understand it?
o: I do not know the word
panel.why: 不一定 means not necessarily.

panel.q: Which response invites the other person to speak?
panel.why: 你呢？ turns the question to them.

teach.model: Use 其实, 不过 and 对了 to move the conversation. To disagree, soften your language with 不太同意 or 不一定. Ask 你呢 to give the other person a turn.

points.ask: How do I give someone a turn?

trip.prompt: Read about turn taking in conversation and note one rule.

stages.title: Formal and informal registers
stages.hook: You talk to a friend and then to a company director. Which words change when you speak formally?
explain: Register is the level of formality. In Mandarin you can choose 你 or the polite 您. Formal phrases include 您贵姓？ (may I ask your surname?), 请多关照 (please look after me), 劳驾 (excuse me, sorry to trouble you) and 拜托您了 (I'm counting on you).

Informal speech uses more particles and slang. A friend may say 哥们儿 (buddy) or ask 吃了吗？ as a casual greeting. Informal talk is shorter, uses 咋 or 啥 in some northern areas, and drops formal connectors.

Written Chinese also has levels. Formal writing prefers two-syllable words, such as 购买 (buy) instead of 买, and uses polite forms like 敬请 (kindly). Choosing the wrong register can sound too cold or too casual, so match the situation and the age of the listener.
stages.mnemonic: Know your listener: 您 for respect, 你 for friends.
items: excuse me, sorry to trouble you
sentences: Excuse me, may I ask your surname?
I would like to ask you a question.

gq.q: Which phrase asks someone's surname politely?
gq.why: 您贵姓 is a polite, formal way to ask.

gq.q: Which word is informal for a friend?

panel.q: Why would a student say 您 to a professor but 你 to a roommate?
o: Because the professor is a different gender
Because it is a different dialect
panel.why: Mandarin uses the polite pronoun to show respect, and 你 for equals.

panel.q: Why is 吃了吗？ not always a question about food?
o: It is an invitation to dinner
It works as a casual greeting
panel.why: It is a friendly greeting, similar to "How are you?"

panel.q: In formal writing, which choice is more suitable?
panel.why: Formal writing prefers more formal words such as 购买.

teach.model: Mandarin has 您 for polite speech and 你 for friends. Formal phrases include 您贵姓 and 请多关照. Informal talk uses slang like 哥们儿. Choose the register to fit the listener.

points.ask: Which word is the polite you?

trip.prompt: Find a definition of register and give one example from your own language.

stages.title: Reading articles and literature
stages.hook: A famous Tang poem tells about moonlight and missing home. Can you read it in Chinese?
explain: Reading Chinese texts means meeting different genres: 新闻 (xīnwén, news), 小说 (xiǎoshuō, novels), 散文 (sǎnwén, prose) and 诗 (shī, poems). News uses clear, compact language and a headline (标题, biāotí). Classical poetry uses very short lines.

The Tang dynasty (618–907) is called the golden age of poetry. 李白 (Lǐ Bái) wrote 静夜思 (Jìng Yè Sī, "Quiet Night Thought"): 床前明月光，疑是地上霜。举头望明月，低头思故乡。 It says: moonlight before my bed, I think it is frost on the ground; I raise my head to look at the moon, lower it and think of home.

Reading tips: look for repeated characters, notice the poem's rhythm (five characters per line here), and use the title to guess the theme. In modern articles, scan the headline first, then the first sentence of each paragraph.
stages.mnemonic: Raise the head to the moon, lower it to home: 举头, 低头.
sentences: Bright moonlight in front of my bed.
I raise my head and look at the bright moon.
I lower my head and think of home.

gq.why: 静夜思 is a famous poem by the Tang poet Li Bai.

gq.q: What does 举头望明月 say?
o: He raises his head and looks at the moon
gq.why: 举头 is raising the head, 望 is to gaze, 明月 is the bright moon.

panel.q: What feeling does the poem express?
panel.why: He sees moonlight and thinks of his hometown.

panel.q: Why is it useful to read the headline of a news article first?
panel.why: The headline summarises the topic, so you can predict the content.

panel.q: Which reading strategy suits a short poem?
panel.why: Notice rhythm and repeated images, and use the title.

teach.model: A Tang poem uses short lines with strong images. In 静夜思, Li Bai sees moonlight on his bed and thinks of home. Reading the title and noticing the images helps understanding.

points.ask: How can I read a poem?

trip.prompt: Read about Li Bai and find another poem about the moon.

stages.title: Essay and correspondence writing
stages.hook: How do you start and end a formal letter in Chinese? The format is quite different from English.
explain: A Chinese formal letter has a greeting, a body and a closing. The first line names the person: 尊敬的王老师： (Respected Teacher Wang). 尊敬的 (zūnjìng de) is formal, and 亲爱的 (qīn'ài de) is for friends or family. Then the first line of the body is indented by two characters.

The body should be clear and polite: 谢谢您的帮助 (thank you for your help). Close with 此致 on one line and 敬礼 on the next, or 祝您工作顺利 (wishing you success at work). A less formal closing is 祝好 (best wishes). Then add the writer's name and the date (落款, luòkuǎn).
An email works the same way but is shorter: a clear subject line, the greeting, the request, a thank you, and 附件 (fùjiàn, attachment). Avoid slang and keep sentences simple and polite.
stages.mnemonic: Dear, body, thanks, wishes, name, date.

gq.q: Which opening suits a letter to a professor?
gq.why: 尊敬的 is the formal opening.
此致敬礼 is used in formal letters.

panel.q: Why do you use 您 and not 你 in a formal email?
panel.why: 您 shows respect to the recipient.

panel.q: What belongs at the end of a letter?
panel.why: The name and date, called 落款, close the letter.

panel.q: Which is an appropriate closing for a friend?
panel.why: 祝好 is friendly and less stiff.

teach.topic: Writing a formal letter in Chinese
teach.model: A formal letter opens with 尊敬的 and the name, has a polite body, and closes with 此致敬礼 or 祝您…. Add your name and date at the end. Use 您 to show respect.

trip.prompt: Find an example of a Chinese letter and spot the greeting and closing.

stages.title: Translation fundamentals
stages.hook: Is translation just replacing each word with another? Try translating 吃了吗？ word for word.
explain: Translation (翻译, fānyì) means conveying meaning, not just words. 直译 (zhíyì) is literal translation, and 意译 (yìyì) is free translation by meaning. 吃了吗？ literally asks "have you eaten?", but in a greeting a better translation is "How are you?"

Context (语境, yǔjìng) decides meaning. The Chinese word 意思 can mean meaning, wish or interesting, depending on the sentence. Differences also exist in grammar: Chinese has no articles or plural endings, so a translator into Chinese must choose natural words, and a translator from Chinese must supply "the" or "a".

Idioms need care. The four-character idiom 画蛇添足 (huà shé tiān zú) means to draw a snake and add feet, that is, to ruin something by adding unnecessary things. Translating it literally confuses readers, so give the meaning, or an equivalent idiom.
stages.mnemonic: Translate the meaning, not the word.
sentences: This word is hard to translate.
We need to look at the context.

gq.why: 意译 is translating the meaning freely.

gq.q: What does 画蛇添足 mean?
o: To add something unnecessary and spoil it
gq.why: It means to spoil something by adding unnecessary parts.

panel.q: Why is "Have you eaten?" not always the best translation of 吃了吗？
o: Because it works as a greeting
panel.why: It is a greeting, so the natural English is "How are you?"

panel.q: What should a translator do when translating Chinese into English about a book?
panel.why: English needs articles and plural forms, so the translator must decide.

panel.q: Why does context matter for the word 意思?
panel.why: Its meaning changes with the sentence.

teach.model: Translation conveys meaning. Literal translation is word for word, and free translation follows meaning. Context decides which meaning of a word is right, and idioms usually need a meaning-based translation.

points.ask: How do I choose between meanings?

trip.prompt: Read about literal and free translation and note one example.

stages.title: Regional varieties and cultural context
stages.hook: Do all Chinese people speak the same? Cantonese, Hokkien and Mandarin differ a lot in speech.
explain: Chinese is a family of varieties that are often not mutually understandable. 粤语 (Yuèyǔ, Cantonese) is spoken in Guangdong, Hong Kong and Macau. 闽南语 (Mǐnnányǔ, Southern Min or Hokkien) is spoken in Fujian, Taiwan and Southeast Asia. 吴语 (Wúyǔ) includes Shanghainese, and 客家话 (Kèjiāhuà) is Hakka.

Speakers of these varieties usually share the same written tradition, but they pronounce characters differently. Cantonese keeps more tones than Mandarin, and has its own romanisation such as Jyutping. 普通话 is used as the common language of education and media in mainland China.

Script is another variation: 简体字 (jiǎntǐzì, simplified) is used in mainland China and Singapore, while 繁體字 (fántǐzì, traditional) is used in Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macau. Whether the varieties are "dialects" or separate languages is debated, since speakers feel one Chinese identity, but linguistically the differences are large.
sentences: People in Hong Kong often speak Cantonese.

gq.q: Which is spoken in Hong Kong?
gq.why: Cantonese (粤语) is widely spoken in Hong Kong and Guangdong.

gq.q: Which script is mostly used in Taiwan?

panel.q: Why is it debated whether Cantonese is a "dialect"?
o: They differ a lot in speech but share a script and identity
panel.why: The varieties differ greatly in speech, but share script and identity.

panel.q: Why can two people who speak different varieties write to each other?
panel.why: They share a common written tradition of characters.

panel.q: What is 普通话 used for?
panel.why: It is the national standard in education and media.

teach.model: Chinese has many varieties such as Cantonese and Hokkien. They share a writing tradition but sound different. Mandarin is the standard in education and media. Simplified and traditional are two sets of characters.

trip.prompt: Find a map of Chinese language groups and note where Cantonese is spoken.

stages.title: Structured debates and presentations
stages.hook: How do you convince an audience in two minutes? A strong opening and a clear structure help.
explain: Presentations and debates need structure. Start with a greeting: 各位老师、同学们，大家好 (hello teachers and classmates). State your position: 我的观点是… (my view is…). Give reasons: 第一…第二…, and finish with 总结 (zǒngjié, summary).
In a debate, you may 支持 (zhīchí, support) or 反对 (fǎnduì, oppose) a motion. Use evidence (论据, lùnjù) and polite words to disagree: 我不同意您的看法，因为… Avoid personal attacks, and focus on arguments.

Speak clearly with tones, use short sentences, and pause between points. Finish by thanking the audience: 谢谢大家聆听 (thank you all for listening). Eye contact and a steady pace make Chinese speeches easier to follow.
stages.mnemonic: Greet, claim, give reasons, sum up, thank.
sentences: My view is that students should read more.
I do not agree with your view.

gq.q: What does 我的观点是 introduce?

panel.q: Why give 论据 in a debate?
panel.why: Evidence supports your claim and persuades the audience.

panel.q: A debater says 你的想法太愚蠢了. What is wrong with that?
o: It is grammatically perfect and polite
It attacks the person, not the argument
panel.why: Attacking the person instead of the argument is impolite and weak.

panel.q: What is a good order for a short speech?
panel.why: Greeting, position, reasons, summary, thanks is a clear order.

teach.model: Start with a greeting, state your view with 我的观点是, give reasons, sum up and thank the audience. In debate, give evidence and disagree politely.

trip.prompt: Read about debate formats and find one that uses supporting and opposing sides.
